title: Pinzimonio
subtitle: Italian raw vegetables with seasoned olive oil for dipping
excerpt: Pinzimonio is the Tuscan and central Italian way of eating raw vegetables: fresh, seasonal vegetables arranged on a platter with individual bowls of extra virgin olive oil seasoned with salt and pepper for dipping. It is one of the simplest things in Italian cooking and one of the most dependent on quality: the olive oil must be very good.
sourceNotes: Pinzimonio is a Tuscan and central Italian tradition, documented in Italian food culture as an antipasto of raw vegetables and seasoned oil. The name derives from the Italian verb pinzare (to clamp or pinch): describing the action of dipping. It is associated particularly with Tuscany, Umbria, and Lazio, where high-quality extra virgin olive oil is produced.

recipe.batchNotes: Add more vegetables in proportion for a larger group.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Prepare the vegetables up to 2 hours ahead and keep in cold water to stay crisp. Drain and dry before serving. Mix the dipping oil just before bringing to the table.

content.text: Pinzimonio asks two things: good vegetables and good olive oil. The oil is not for drizzling over the vegetables but for individual bowls at each place setting, each person seasoning their own with salt and pepper and dipping as they eat. Use your best extra virgin olive oil. A flat, mild oil will make the dish taste of nothing; a peppery, green Tuscan oil makes it taste of summer.

items.prepNote: cut into wedges through the core
with a little green stalk left on
freshly ground, for the dipping bowls

content.text: Cut all the vegetables into pieces that are easy to hold and dip: fennel into wedges, celery into sticks with leaves attached, carrots and courgettes into batons about 10 cm long and 1.5 cm wide. Radishes can be left whole or halved.
If preparing ahead, place the cut vegetables in a bowl of cold water to keep them crisp and to prevent the cut surfaces from oxidising. Drain and dry thoroughly before serving.

Arrange the vegetables on a large platter or in a bowl. Pour the olive oil into 4 small individual bowls: one per person. Each person seasons their own oil with salt and pepper, then dips and eats. Bring bread alongside for the oil.

items.symptom: Vegetables are limp and not crisp
items.cause: Cut too far ahead without being kept in cold water, or left at room temperature too long
items.fix: Cut and submerge in cold water up to 2 hours ahead. Dry very well before serving: wet vegetables won't hold the oil on their surface.

items.symptom: Oil tastes flat and doesn't carry the vegetables
items.cause: Low-quality or old olive oil used
items.fix: Pinzimonio is not the place for light or cheap olive oil. Use your best peppery extra virgin oil, ideally a Tuscan or Umbrian harvest-season oil.

content.text: Pinzimonio is a Tuscan antipasto tradition. It is best in autumn when the new season's olive oil is fresh and peppery. In Tuscany it is eaten at the start of a meal alongside bruschetta and sliced meats. It is also eaten as an afternoon snack. The oil is the dish: everything else is just a vehicle for it.
